newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close sharply lower on Hanbo crisis.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close sharply lower on Hanbo crisis.

text.p: The political community's move to take up the Hanbo Group's financial crisis as a political issue sent stocks to a sharply lower close on Monday, brokers said.
President Kim Young-sam's ruling party on Monday conceded to opposition demands for a parliamentary probe into the financial affairs of the country's 14th largest industrial conglomerate.
The composite index shed 2.98 percent, or 20.41 points, to close at a provisional 664.70.
"The political community's move sparked renewed concerns that the issue could develop into a much more complicated one," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.

The market rose on Friday and Saturday as investors shrugged off the long-term impact from Hanbo's debt default on Thursday. But brokers said investors have begun taking the situation more seriously following the political community's action.

Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of the conglomerate, defaulted on debt repayments on Thursday. Its main creditor bank said the group was expected to apply for court receivership for Hanbo Steel and three other units of the group on Monday or Tuesday.

Asset-rich stocks were among the few gainers helped by a rotationing buying interest. Dong Won Co closed at its daily upper limit of 49,500 won by gaining 3,600 won and Pang Rim Co rose 2,400 won to 42,400.
The index futures March contracts shed 2.95 points to 66.90 while the base KOSPI-200 index fell 2.13 points to 69.38.
